The telescope cost nine billion dollars. It took twenty-five years to build. On Christmas morning, it launched into space on a column of fire. Six months later, it sent back its first image. The photograph showed galaxies thirteen billion years old. Light that had been traveling since before the Earth existed. The scientists at mission control stood in silence. Some of them had spent their entire careers waiting for this moment. Dr. Chen, the lead engineer, was sixty-three. She started working on the project at thirty-eight. Her daughter grew up hearing about it at the dinner table. Now her daughter is an astrophysicist too. The image changed our understanding of the early universe overnight. It will take decades to fully process what it revealed. Nine billion dollars is a lot of money. But some things are worth the price. Knowing where we came from is one of them.
